title: audit current LEET
purpose: Ground truth only. No change proposed. This is the factual baseline for the follow-on fix tasks.
headline: LEET is NOT a token dictionary: it is a single character-to-character str.maketrans table of 10 entries / 8 distinct canonical values at normalize.py:256, applied at exactly ONE call site (normalize.py:280), per whole name token, name field only, with NO country in scope. The confirmed French-ordinal defect therefore cannot be fixed inside the table. The fix belongs at the CALL SITE in _name_tokens. TWO NEW DEFECTS found that the brief's proposed ordinal guard would MISS: 24hr->2ahr (US, 3657) and 1st->lst (US 679 + India 381 = 1060).

most_important_number.meaning: total corrupted name-token occurrences across all 6 profile files, of which the brief's proposed guard ^\d+(e|er|ere|eme)$ catches only 1111 (19.1%)
most_important_number.denominator: 176142 mixed letter+digit name-token occurrences, all 6 files, 3 countries
most_important_number.source: name_tokens[country] restricted to tokens matching [a-z].*[0-9]|[0-9].*[a-z], in all 6 analysis_out/profile/*.json

leet_table_exact_contents.self_maps_note: No key equals its value, and the value space (letters) is disjoint from the key space (digits+symbols), so the table is single-pass and non-cascading. The 'missing self-map' concept from the token-dictionary tables (US_STATES etc) does NOT transfer to LEET.

call_site.repo_wide_search: LEET|translate(|maketrans over all 19 .py files under _upstream returns EXACTLY TWO hits, both in normalize.py
call_site.granularity: per-token, whole-token pass (str.translate rewrites every character of the token; there is no regex, no anchoring, no boundary logic)
call_site.address_evidence: normalize_address (normalize.py:314-353) never references LEET; its tokens go to canon.get(t, t) at normalize.py:347
call_site.trigger_condition: fires only when the token contains BOTH a letter and a digit (normalize.py:279); pure-digit or pure-alpha tokens are never translated
call_site.country_evidence: normalize_name(raw) at normalize.py:285 has no country parameter and prep.py:12 does not supply one, whereas normalize_address(raw, country) at normalize.py:314 does take one and uses it at lines 318/321/337. Country is therefore not in scope anywhere on the LEET path.
call_path: normalize.py:279  if any(c.isalpha() for c in t) and any(c.isdigit() for c in t):
normalize.py:280  t = t.translate(LEET)   <-- THE ONLY APPLICATION

ordering.implication_for_fix: A NAME_CANON entry keyed on the literal '3eme' could NEVER fire today, because line 281 already sees 'eeme'. Any guard must run BEFORE line 280 if a NAME_CANON ordinal entry is also wanted.

call_site.downstream_blast_radius: ncore is built from core (normalize.py:306) and feeds keys.py:33-34. keys.py:42 filters ADDRESS tokens with ~str.contains(r'^\d+$'), but name tokens enter nt unfiltered at length>=2, so a corrupted name token like 'eeme' becomes a live blocking key while the same business's address side keeps the correct '3eme'.

per_token_not_per_substring.question: is LEET applied per-token or per-substring, and does the guard need rewriting?
per_token_not_per_substring.answer: per-token, whole-token, single-pass. str.translate rewrites every character; values are never keys so nothing cascades.

measured_repeated_leet_key.meaning: Across all 284 mixed token types in all 6 files, ZERO contain a repeated leet key. So translate rewrites exactly one character in every observed case.

per_token_not_per_substring.implication: A whole-token-anchored guard ^...$ is the correct shape. An unanchored/substring guard would be wrong in principle even though it is indistinguishable on current data.

denominator.definition: name_tokens[country] in all 6 profile JSONs, restricted to tokens containing at least one letter AND at least one digit (the normalize.py:279 trigger)
denominator.caveat: name_tokens is pruned to top-4000 per country by build_profile.py, so these are LOWER BOUNDS, not complete enumerations.

D1_french_ordinals.status: CONFIRMED, reproduced independently from the raw profile files

N1_24hr_NEW.why_wrong: '24hr' is the standard abbreviation for 24 hours. The 4 is a real digit, not a leet stand-in, and 2 is not even a LEET key, so the token is mangled into '2ahr', which is not a word in any language in this dataset.
N1_24hr_NEW.rank: 2nd-largest single mixed type in the entire dataset

family_size.note: the family is exactly one token, not a class

N1_24hr_NEW.why_not: it ends in 'hr', not in an ordinal suffix

N2_1st_NEW.why_wrong: '1st' is the ordinary English ordinal; LEET maps 1->l. Same pattern as the French ordinals, in two more countries.
N2_1st_NEW.why_not: it is an English ordinal, not a French one

broader_family.absence_caveat: NOT in the top-4000 name_tokens is not proof of absence; the list is truncated.

control_case.meaning: contains 2, which is NOT a LEET key, so it passes through unchanged and correct. This proves the corruption is caused specifically by the 1->l key, not merely by the presence of a leading digit.

address_side_occurrences.note: all preserved verbatim because normalize_address never calls LEET

defects.N2_asymmetry_significance: For 1st alone: 1060 corrupted name occurrences against 321834 preserved address occurrences. keys.py:33 builds name keys from the LEET-processed ncore while keys.py:39-43 builds address keys from unprocessed atoks, and the kind-0 key at keys.py:60 XORs the two. A business whose name contains '1st' therefore cannot match a business whose address contains '1st'. This is the mechanism by which the defect costs matches, not just dirty tokens.

D3_dead_keys_NEW.status: NEW DEFECT (cosmetic, zero behavioural impact), CONFIRMED by construction
D3_dead_keys_NEW.claim: @->a and $->s are PROVABLY UNREACHABLE in the current pipeline.
D3_dead_keys_NEW.proof: _name_tokens splits on _non_alnum at normalize.py:276, and _non_alnum = re.compile(r'[^a-z0-9]+') at normalize.py:269. By the time normalize.py:280 runs, the token is guaranteed to contain only [a-z0-9], so a character-level lookup for @ or $ can never hit. A search for [@$] across normalize.py returns ONLY line 256 - no earlier step maps @ or $ to a letter.
D3_dead_keys_NEW.behavioural_impact: none - harmless, costs nothing and corrupts nothing
D3_dead_keys_NEW.why_still_worth_reporting: misleading: a maintainer reading the table believes symbol-leetspeak is handled
D3_dead_keys_NEW.resolves_D090_gap: D090 recorded '@ and $ cannot be evaluated at all' as a GAP. It is resolved here: not merely unmeasurable, but unreachable by construction. The same blindness applies at profile time - build_profile.py:28 TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r'[a-z0-9]+') discards symbols, so no measurement could ever have found them.

D4_4l_RESOLVED_NOT_A_DEFECT.resolves: D090 left '4l' unresolved (1943 occurrences, its largest French mixed type)
D4_4l_RESOLVED_NOT_A_DEFECT.resolution: 4l->al and India's a1->al (272) CONVERGE on the same output. 'al' is an ordinary token (Al / Albert). So 4l behaves as a CORRECT leet expansion of 'al', not a corruption. It is NOT part of the 1111.
D4_4l_RESOLVED_NOT_A_DEFECT.evidence_strength: inference from output convergence, NOT a raw-data read (raw data access is forbidden by the hard constraints)

many_to_one_collisions.assessment: almost all are DESIRABLE many-to-one merges - that is the entire point of the table (5ervices+s0lutions+so1utions -> solutions; 8rothers+br0thers -> brothers). These are the regression set the fix must not break.

empty_string_values.note: all 10 values are single characters. For contrast, ADDR_CANON_COMMON DOES carry 13 empty mappings ('number': '' etc, normalize.py:196-197) - a different mechanism: token deletion, consumed downstream at keys.py:39.

missing_self_maps.note: No LEET key equals its value, and the value space (a,b,e,g,l,o,s,t) is disjoint from the key space (digits+symbols), so the table is idempotent-safe and non-recursive. The 'missing self-map' concept from the token-dictionary tables (US_STATES etc) does NOT transfer to LEET - it is a character map, not a lookup dict.

overlap_with_ADDR_CANON_COMMON.proof: LEET is only ever applied at normalize.py:280 inside _name_tokens; ADDR_CANON_COMMON is only ever consulted at normalize.py:347 inside normalize_address. The two tables sit on DISJOINT code paths and can never see the same token. Any audit that treats them as potentially interacting is wrong. Note ADDR_CANON_COMMON does contain first->1st, second->2nd, third->3rd at normalize.py:184 - English ordinals as ADDRESS values - but those are address-side and never meet LEET.

unmapped_digits.evidence: only 2 of 284 mixed token types contain 2 or 9 (24hr 3657, 2nd 253), and both are corrupted for a different reason.

fix_location_verdict.answer: THE CALL SITE (_name_tokens, normalize.py:279-280). NOT the table.
fix_location_verdict.reason_1_structural: LEET is str.maketrans, a character->character map (normalize.py:256). The defect needs the WHOLE token to decide whether to fire. A character map has no context and cannot express 'skip this token'. The information required is strictly more than a per-character table can hold.
fix_location_verdict.reason_2_empirical: Deleting a key does not work. Measured sole-dependency mass per key (tokens whose ONLY leet key present is that digit): 0=71527, 1=47775, 5=33541, 8=9195, 6=7373, 4=5600, 3=869, 7=9. Removing 1 to save 1st (1060) would break de1hi (1674), denta1 (1652), techno1ogies (1288) and 82 other types. Removing 4 to save 24hr (3657) would break 4l (1943). EVERY KEY IS LOAD-BEARING.
fix_location_verdict.reason_3_country_impossible_and_wrong: Country is not in scope on this path at all (signature normalize.py:285, call site prep.py:12). And a country guard would be the wrong shape anyway: N1 and N2 are US and INDIA defects. A French-only guard fixes 1111 of 5828.
fix_location_verdict.conclusion: A guard predicate at the call site, immediately before normalize.py:280, keyed on the whole token. Per per_token_not_per_substring it must be token-anchored (^...$).
fix_location_verdict.constraint_on_the_fix: The guard must EXEMPT rather than EXTEND. 170314 of 176142 observed mixed occurrences (96.7%) are correct leet expansions; any change must be a no-op on those. c1ub->club and mais0n->maison are the named regression cases. Also, a NAME_CANON entry keyed '3eme' cannot work today because normalize.py:281 already sees 'eeme' - the guard must run BEFORE line 280 if a NAME_CANON ordinal entry is also wanted.
fix_location_verdict.status: JUDGEMENT ONLY - no change proposed, per the work order

gaps: addr_tokens is also top-4000 and count>=2 per country (build_profile.py:126-127, 141). Address-side masses in N2 are LOWER BOUNDS, and the top-4000 cap means a literal absent from addr_tokens is NOT proven absent.

~8-10% of name-token mass is outside the top-4000 cut. All type-level lists here (284 types) are floors, not complete enumerations. The 284 / 176142 figures are 'observed within the top-4000', not 'total in the data'.

NO PROFILE FIELD COUNTS HOW MANY ROWS A GIVEN TOKEN TYPE APPEARS IN - only token occurrences. The per-row impact of the 5828 corrupted occurrences is NOT DERIVABLE from the profile. Do not quote a row count for the ordinal defect.
No raw-data check was possible or attempted (hard constraint). The 4l resolution is inferred from output convergence with a1->al, not from a source-data read.
Country-level 'rows' is absent for France in all three train files (by_country has no France key). France is test-only, as D090 already established.
not_rederived: REFUTED-1 France postal codes lost by the pin guard
US_STATES / IN_STATES / FR_REGIONS need no dictionary expansion
France blocking caps are healthy (99.94% survive S1_MAXCAP=300)
address component order is not a problem
ligature deletion and inline-postcode losses are negligible for scoring
